clue.text: A piece of cake one left inside mug

indicators.note: inside means the following letters go within the word for mug

parts.note: mug is slang for face
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a slice of cake in a cup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A piece of cake' looks like a literal slice of cake left in a mug; it is the definition, meaning something easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of cake is an idiom for an easy task, and facile means easily achieved.

clue.text: One petrified girl is so frantic to keep up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the kept letters are read from the bottom upwards
the words girl is so frantic keep a run of letters within them, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A frightened young woman is so panicked that she cannot keep pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' holds LISSOF inside 'girL IS SO Frantic', and 'up' turns it round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the remains of a creature turned to stone, literally one petrified.

clue.text: Duty on industry perhaps to have copy press are demanding

indicators.note: in a down clue the copy is pressed on top of the next piece, as a carbon sheet sits on the page

parts.note: a carbon is a carbon copy
things that tax us are demanding of us

explanation.surface: A levy on business lets the newspapers insist on having duplicates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' places CARBON above TAX in the down light, with a nod to how a carbon copy is made by pressing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon tax is a levy on emissions, typically charged to industry, so it is an example of such a duty.

clue.text: Creature that was part of the house that Jacques built?

definitions.text: Creature that was part of the house that Jacques built?

parts.words: Creature that was part of the house that Jacques built?
parts.note: the house that Jack built becomes a Frenchman's house, and a part of a house in French, the wall with its article, gives a primate's name

explanation.surface: A riddle about which animal featured in the nursery rhyme house, told with a French Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Le mur' is French for 'the wall', a part of any house; the question mark flags the French split.
explanation.definitionFit: The lemur is a Madagascan primate, so the clue's creature is this animal in disguise.

clue.text: Mark left outside yard made by panda perhaps

indicators.note: outside means the mark's letters go round the word for yard

parts.note: a scar is a mark left behind by a wound
a quad is a quadrangle, a college or school yard

explanation.surface: Someone scuffed the edge of a courtyard, and a panda is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'panda' or panda car is British slang for a small police patrol car, once painted in panda-like blocks of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda car is an example of a police patrol vehicle, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Tho' seeming to change, at first leave a lot to be desired

indicators.note: at first places the word for leave in front of the rearranged letters

parts.note: to quit is to leave

indicators.note: to change says the letters of Tho' seeming are rearranged

explanation.surface: An observation that something appearing to change still leaves a lot to be desired.
explanation.walkthrough: The familiar phrase 'leave a lot to be desired' hides the split: 'leave' belongs to the wordplay and 'at first' puts it in front, so the definition is only the closing words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable is a lot to be desired, an impressive thing worth wanting.

clue.text: Wondering where young man should go in a brawl?

indicators.note: in means the young man's destination goes inside the brawl

parts.note: a ruck is a rough brawl or scrum
'Go west, young man' is the famous advice to young Americans

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about where a young lad ought to head during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west, young man' is a famous piece of advice to young Americans heading for the frontier; the question mark flags this allusive way of giving a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awestruck is filled with wonder, so wondering is a looser synonym.

clue.text: Brussels intertwined with Auntie's climbing plant

indicators.note: intertwined with says the union's letters and the broadcaster's letters are woven together into a new order

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, standing for the union
Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: Brussels sprouts tangled up with a relative's climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is a British nickname for the BBC. The blog reads the weave as alternate letters then turned up the light; mixing EU and BBC gives the same five letters, leaving 'climbing plant' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubeb is a climbing pepper vine of Java whose berries are used as a spice.

clue.text: Upset, mothers instantly disavow our gutless, yobbish behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read upwards
gutless says each of the four words loses its insides, keeping just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Mothers are upset, instantly disowning our cowardly loutish conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' keeps MS, IY, DW, OR from the four words, and 'Upset' reverses MSIYDWOR in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is loud, disorderly conduct, the sort of behaviour expected of a yob or lout.

clue.text: Pants on run, encouraging son to keep behind!

indicators.note: to keep means the two pieces hold the backside between them

parts.note: jogging someone is nudging or prompting them on
the behind is the bottom

explanation.surface: Trousers worn while running, cheering a boy to stay at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underwear but here means trousers, as in American use; 'jogging' a person is prompting them, hence encouraging.
explanation.definitionFit: These are loose tracksuit trousers worn for running, so pants for a run.

clue.text: Volcanic island resort booms 'til end of summer

indicators.note: resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again
end of picks the final letter of summer

explanation.surface: A holiday resort is busy right up to the close of summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but means sort again: BOOMS, TIL and the R from 'end of summer' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is an active volcanic island off Sicily.

clue.text: Barge returning with nobles inside

indicators.note: returning means the assembled letters are read backwards
inside picks the inner letters of nobles, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A barge heads back carrying aristocrats aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' takes OBLE from nobles; W then OBLE is reversed by 'returning'. 'Barge' is a verb, not a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow is to push or barge one's way through.

clue.text: Language is primitive instinct, nothing more

indicators.note: more means another piece is added on after the first

parts.note: the id is the primitive instinctive part of the mind in Freud
O is the zero symbol for nothing

explanation.surface: Language is merely primal urge and nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing more' reads as a phrase meaning 'merely', but splits into O plus 'more' to add it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial language developed from Esperanto.

clue.text: I'm afraid to put good pound back in bank

indicators.note: in means the following letters go inside the word for bank

parts.note: to bank on is to rely

indicators.note: back means the word for pound is read backwards

parts.note: to pound is to batter

explanation.surface: An apologetic remark about returning a good pound coin to the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' and 'pound' look like money but are both verbs: to bank on is to rely, to pound is to batter.
explanation.definitionFit: I'm afraid is a polite phrase of regret, so an adverb meaning sadly fits.

clue.text: Pole's fate sadly sealed by two others

indicators.note: sealed by means the rearranged letters are enclosed between two others

parts.note: S and N are the South and North poles, the other poles

indicators.note: sadly signals that fate's letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A Polish man's destiny unhappily settled by a couple of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality only, but it also prompts the poles S and N enclosing TEFA, the anagram of fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stefan is a common Polish man's first name, so a Pole is named here.

clue.text: Bamboozle harbour administrators with new map

parts.note: to floor someone is to baffle or bamboozle them
the PLA is the Port of London Authority

explanation.surface: Port officials are confused by a new chart.
explanation.walkthrough: The PLA (Port of London Authority) runs the tidal Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor plan is a scale map of a building's layout.

clue.text: Museum's not the first to store English works

indicators.note: to store means the shortened museum holds the next letter
not the first drops the opening letter of the museum name

parts.note: the Louvre's is the possessive of the Paris museum

explanation.surface: A museum other than the leading one keeps English pieces of art.
explanation.walkthrough: The LOUVRE'S loses its L ('not the first') and stores E.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvres are an artist's or writer's works, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Reunited viewers' movement devised plot for Eastenders

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement, a movement of the eyes, our viewers

indicators.note: London East Enders traditionally drop their aitches

parts.note: to hatch a plot is to devise it

explanation.surface: A soap-opera reunion engineered by a scheming storyline for the BBC show.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in East London, and its Cockney speakers drop the H; REM stands for rapid eye movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rematched means paired up again, much like reunited.

clue.text: Given axe, did battle

definitions.meaning: given the axe means abandoned or cancelled, thrown on the heap
to fight is to have a scrap

explanation.definitionFit: Scrapped means discarded, and also fought, from scrap as slang for a fight.

clue.text: Dandy in depression cross and cold

indicators.note: in means the following letters are put into the word for depression

parts.note: a coomb is a valley or hollow in the hillside
X is a cross

explanation.surface: A fop sits gloomy, irritated and chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' and 'cross' look like moods; they are a valley (COOMB) and the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a vain, showy man, a dated synonym for a fop.

clue.text: Agree finally perhaps to take cream round, and cold tongue

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of Agree

parts.note: one might skim milk to take off the cream
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An agreement reached at last, maybe over cream, with a chilled tongue dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold tongue' looks like a deli dish; it is a language spoken in the cold Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Eskimo is a language of the Arctic peoples, a tongue from a cold region.

clue.text: Place restriction on China's foreign correspondent

parts.note: to pen is to confine or restrict
china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Imposing limits on China's overseas journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is capitalised to suggest the country; in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is someone abroad one writes letters to, a foreign correspondent of sorts.

clue.text: A new park pitch covering area becomes official

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters go around the letter for area
new signals that park pitch is made anew in different order

explanation.surface: A fresh park pitch spread over an area gets formal approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PARKPITCH round A for area, all after the first A. 'becomes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparatchik is a party bureaucrat, a functionary or official.

clue.text: Quietly snoring? At heart there's a vivaciousness

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: at heart means the next letter sits in the middle of the snoring sound

parts.note: ZZZ is the cartoon sound of snoring

explanation.surface: Asleep and snoring softly, yet deep down full of life.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeper's sound ZZZ holds A in its middle, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pzazz is a variant spelling of pizzazz, meaning lively flair or vivaciousness.

clue.text: Raised fine up-and-coming actors without a director

explanation.walkthrough: OK upwards gives KO; RADA (a London drama school) drops one A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Korda was a Hungarian-born British film director and producer.

clue.text: Get even Bond girl wearing this? Unlikely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond girl' suggests a James Bond film actress, but Bond is a definition by itself, followed by a cryptic comment on neckwear.

clue.text: It forms in shell or around shell-like place

clue.text: Having exceptional shin power

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters go out of their order

explanation.surface: Possessing extraordinary leg strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of possessing, which is having in noun form.

clue.text: Wanting to go to bed after twelve seconds hugging in ecstasy

explanation.walkthrough: DOZ and SS hug IN and E, the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Doziness is sleepiness, the state of wanting to go to bed.

clue.text: German scorer's name announced on radio

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name
